explanation: Ezra 7:1

question: Which apostle is described as "doubting"?

question: Who suggested that Joseph interpret the dreams of Pharaoh?

question: What are the names of Joseph's two sons?

question: How long did Moses's mother hide him to escape the death edict of Pharaoh?

question: Who was the chief of the three mighty men of David?

question: By whom were the children of Israel carried captive into Assyria?

question: What king's name meant peaceable?

question: What king did God smite with leprosy?
explanation: 2 Chronicles 26:19--21 — "Then Uzziah became furious ... leprosy broke out on his forehead ... So King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death."

question: What king of Israel followed heathen practices by burning his children in the fire?
explanation: 2 Chronicles 28:3 — "He burned incense in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, and burned his children in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations."

question: What is the whole duty of man, according to the Scriptures?

options.label: D

question: How many Philistines did Samson slay with a jaw bone?

question: What was the garden of Eden guarded with to prevent future access to the tree of life?

options.label: B

question: What is the first city mentioned in the Bible?
answer_text: Enoch - built by Cain and named after his son (Genesis 4:17)
explanation: Genesis 4:17 — "And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he built a city, and called the name of the city after the name of his son — Enoch."

question: Of what wood was Noah's Ark made?
explanation: Genesis 6:14 — "Make yourself an ark of gopherwood; make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and outside with pitch."

question: What does Paul say is the fulfillment of the law?

question: How were the children of Israel guided in their forty years of wandering in the wilderness?

question: What were Solomon's other names?

question: Who was the first recorded person raised from death to life?

options.label: D

answer_text: The son of the widow of Zarephath, raised by Elijah (1 Kings 17:21-22)

question: Who delivered Israel by killing 600 Philistines with an ox goad?

question: Who was compelled to bear the cross of Christ to the place of crucifixion?
explanation: Mark 15:21 — "Then they compelled a certain man, Simon a Cyrenian, the father of Alexander and Rufus, as he was coming out of the country and passing by, to bear His cross."

question: What man of Israel was stoned for blaspheming God?

explanation: Leviticus 24:10--14, 23 — "Now the Israelite woman's son blasphemed the name of the Lord and cursed ... So they stoned him with stones."

question: What is the name of the city to which Lot escaped at the destruction of Sodom?
explanation: Genesis 19:22--23 — "Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar. The sun had risen upon the earth when Lot entered Zoar."

question: How old was Moses when he gave God's message to Pharaoh: "Let my people go"?
explanation: Exodus 7:7 — "Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh."

question: Where was Moses buried?
answer_text: In a valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth Peor; no one knows the exact place (Deuteronomy 34:6)
explanation: Deuteronomy 34:6 — "And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth Peor; but no one knows his grave to this day."

question: When Saul was pursuing David, in which cave did David seek refuge?
explanation: 1 Samuel 22:1 — "David therefore departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam."

question: Who restored Paul's sight after the Lord blinded him?
explanation: Acts 9:17--18 — "Ananias went his way and entered the house ... And immediately there fell from his eyes something like scales, and he received his sight at once."

question: Where was Paul stoned?
explanation: Acts 14:19 — "Then Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there; and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing him to be dead."

question: Who partook of a meal prepared by an angel, and was sustained forty days and nights while in the mountain?
answer_text: Elijah - the angel provided food that sustained him 40 days and nights on Mount Horeb (1 Kings 19:5-9)
explanation: 1 Kings 19:5--9 — "So he arose, and ate and drank; and he went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights as far as Horeb, the mountain of God."

question: Who was the servant of the church in Cenchrea?
explanation: Romans 16:1 — "I commend to you Phoebe our sister, who is a servant of the church in Cenchrea."

question: Which three men, in different periods, stood almost alone in their godliness, among a crooked and perverse generation?
explanation: Ezekiel 14:14 — "Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver only themselves by their righteousness."

question: What man, although warned, invited his murderer to a feast?
answer_text: Gedaliah, who invited Ishmael to a feast despite being warned (Jeremiah 40:13-16; 41:1-2)

question: Which two men hid in a well to save their lives?

question: Flee ________
explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:18 — "Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a man does is outside the body, but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body."

question: Who was the first Christian convert in Europe?
answer_text: Lydia, a seller of purple from Thyatira, converted at Philippi (Acts 16:14-15)
explanation: Acts 16:14--15 — "Now a certain woman named Lydia heard us. She was a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira ... The Lord opened her heart to heed the things spoken by Paul."

question: At King Herod's birthday party, what unusual gift did he grant his stepdaughter?

options.label: A
options.text: The head of John the Baptist

answer_text: The head of John the Baptist
explanation: Matthew 14:6--11; Mark 6:21--28 — "The head of John the Baptist" was granted to Herodias's daughter after she danced at Herod's birthday feast.

question: Which governor of Egypt appointed by Pharaoh was responsible for managing the food supply during the seven years of famine?
explanation: Genesis 41:41; 42:6 — "Pharaoh said to Joseph, See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt ... Now Joseph was governor over the land; and it was he who sold to all the people of the land."

question: Name the first two apostles to follow Jesus.
explanation: Matthew 4:18--20 — "And Jesus, walking by the Sea of Galilee, saw two brothers, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea ... They immediately left their nets and followed Him."

question: Which governor of Persia allowed Nehemiah to return to Jerusalem to rebuild the walls of the city?
explanation: Nehemiah 2:1--8 — "And it came to pass in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes ... So it pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time." Artaxerxes I permitted Nehemiah's return.

question: Who said: "If I speak in the tongues of men or of angels, but do not have love, I am only a resounding gong or a clanging cymbal."?
explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:1 — "Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal." Written by the Apostle Paul.

question: Can flesh and blood inherit the kingdom of God? "flesh and blood" cannot inherit the kingdom of God. 1 Corinthians 15:50- "I declare to you, brothers and sisters, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable."

options.text: Yes, flesh and blood can inherit the kingdom of God.

question: According to 2 Corinthians 1:5, what do believers share abundantly in through Christ?

question: Who was the governor of Syria during the census that led Mary and Joseph to Bethlehem?

question: Which verse discusses the judgment seat of Christ where everyone will receive what is due for their actions, whether good or bad?
explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:10 — "For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad."

question: Which of the following is the focus of Paul's boast in Galatians 6:14?

options.label: B

answer_text: The cross of our Lord Jesus Christ
explanation: Galatians 6:14 — "But God forbid that I should boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ."

question: Which book of the Bible says, "Let all the earth fear the Lord; let all the people of the world revere him"?

question: In 2 Corinthians, who was the governor in Damascus who tried to arrest Paul ?

question: Who was the Apostle who was let down in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped from the Damascenes?

question: According to 2 Timothy 3:16, who is the ultimate author of Scripture?
explanation: 2 Timothy 3:16 — "All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine."

question: Who became bitter and said, "Call me Mara"?
explanation: Ruth 1:20 — "But she said to them, Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me."

question: According to Galatians 5:16, what should you do to avoid gratifying the desires of the flesh?

question: What was the name of Deborah's husband in the Bible?
explanation: Judges 4:4 — "Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, was judging Israel at that time."

question: Who was Samson's father?
explanation: Judges 13:2, 24 — "There was a certain man from Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah ... So the woman bore a son and called his name Samson."

question: Who rose above his brothers' jealousy and became a ruler in Egypt?

question: Which prophet was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, rising above earthly life?
explanation: 2 Kings 2:11 — "Then it happened, as they continued on and talked, that suddenly a chariot of fire appeared with horses of fire ... and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven."

question: Who rose above his physical blindness to see Jesus' miracles and became a follower?

question: Who said, "I am chief of sinners"?

question: Who is the head of the body, the church?

question: In the Book of Amos, the prophet speaks of a coming famine. What kind of famine does he describe?

question: According to Proverbs 18:10, what is the name of the Lord compared to?

question: Is Covetousness, idolatry?

question: According to 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17, who will rise first at the Second Coming of Jesus?

question: According to 1 Thessalonians 5:9, what did God appoint us to receive through our Lord Jesus Christ?
explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:9 — "For God did not appoint us to wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ."

question: According to the Bible, how long was the journey from Egypt to the Promised Land supposed to take?
explanation: Deuteronomy 1:2 — "It is eleven days' journey from Horeb by way of Mount Seir to Kadesh Barnea." The direct route to the Promised Land was only eleven days.

question: Who is Timothy's mother?
explanation: 2 Timothy 1:5 — "When I call to remembrance the genuine faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice."

question: From which lineage is Jesus Christ descended?
explanation: Romans 1:3; Matthew 1:1 — "The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the Son of David."

question: Did Timothy in the Bible have any health problems?
explanation: 1 Timothy 5:23 — "No longer drink only water, but use a little wine for your stomach's sake and your frequent infirmities."

question: Who tasted death for everyone? Options
explanation: Hebrews 2:9 — "But we see Jesus ... that He, by the grace of God, might taste death for everyone."

question: Who was without sin in the Bible?
explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:21; Hebrews 4:15 — "For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us." Jesus was without sin.

question: How did Jesus learn obedience?
explanation: Hebrews 5:8 though He was a Son, yet He learned obedience by the things which He suffered.

question: What does God promise in Jeremiah 33:3?
explanation: Jeremiah 33:3 — "Call to Me, and I will answer you, and show you great and mighty things, which you do not know."

question: "Therefore do not cast away your confidence, which has great reward." This verse is found in which book of the Bible?
explanation: Hebrews 10:35 Therefore do not cast away your confidence, which has great reward.

question: According to James 1:3, what does the testing of your faith produce?
explanation: James 1:3 — "Knowing that the testing of your faith produces patience."

question: Where in the Bible do we find the verse, "But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy."?
explanation: James 3:17 — "But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy."

question: Therefore, to him who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is ____.
answer_text: Sin - "To him who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin" (James 4:17)
explanation: James 4:17 — "Therefore, to him who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin."

question: For how long did Elijah stop the rain?
explanation: James 5:17 — "Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain; and it did not rain on the land for three years and six months."

question: In Luke 23:28, what did Jesus tell the "Daughters of Jerusalem" to do?
explanation: Luke 23:28 — "But Jesus, turning to them, said, Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children."

question: How many souls were saved during the time of Noah's Ark? Options
explanation: 1 Peter 3:20; Genesis 7:13 — "The Divine longsuffering waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water."

question: What is reserved for fire until the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men?
explanation: 2 Peter 3:7 — "But the heavens and the earth which are now preserved by the same word, are reserved for fire until the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men."

question: Who is our advocate with the Father?
explanation: 1 John 2:1 — "And if anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous."

question: According to Isaiah 38:18, what cannot praise or thank God?
explanation: Isaiah 38:18 — "For Sheol cannot thank You, death cannot praise You; those who go down to the pit cannot hope for Your truth."

question: On which island did John have a vision of the Lord's day?
explanation: Revelation 1:9 — "I, John ... was on the island that is called Patmos for the word of God and for the testimony of Jesus Christ."

question: Give reference of Seven Spirits of the Lord
explanation: Isaiah 11:2 — "The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon Him: the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord."

question: To which church was this said: "So then, because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will vomit you out of My mouth"?
explanation: Revelation 3:16 — "So then, because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will vomit you out of My mouth." (Letter to Laodicea.)

question: In Revelation 5:4, who is the "I" who wept because no one was found worthy to open and read the scroll?
explanation: Revelation 5:4 — "So I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open and read the scroll, or to look at it." John, the author of Revelation, is the "I."

question: According to Psalm 119:71, why was it good for the psalmist to be afflicted?
explanation: Psalm 119:71 — "It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn Your statutes."

question: In the book of Revelation, what do the "seven lamps of fire" represent?
explanation: Revelation 4:5

question: Who has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seals?
explanation: Revelation 5:5 — "Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals."

question: Who can stand the great day of the Lord's wrath?

options.label: A
options.text: The righteous by their own deeds

explanation: Revelation 6:17; 7:14 — "For the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand? ... These are the ones who come out of the great tribulation."

question: Whose power is described as being "in their mouth and in their tails; for their tails are like serpents, having heads; and with them they do harm"?

options.label: D
options.text: The Horses of the Sixth Trumpet

answer_text: The Horses of the Sixth Trumpet
explanation: Revelation 9:19 — "For their power is in their mouth and in their tails; for their tails are like serpents, having heads; and with them they do harm." (The horses of the sixth trumpet.)

question: What were the three plagues by which a third of mankind was killed?

options.label: B
options.text: Water Turning to Blood, Frogs, Flies

explanation: Revelation 9:18 — "By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed — by the fire and the smoke and the brimstone which came out of their mouths."

question: By how many plagues was a third of mankind killed?
explanation: Revelation 9:18 — "By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed."

question: What happened when the first angel poured out his bowl upon the earth who had the mark of the beast and worshipped his image?

options.label: B
options.text: a foul and loathsome sore came

explanation: Revelation 16:2 — "So the first went and poured out his bowl upon the earth, and a foul and loathsome sore came upon the men who had the mark of the beast."

question: "Behold, I am coming as a _____. Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame."
explanation: Revelation 16:15

question: Complete the verse: "And anyone not found written in the ________ was cast into the lake of fire."
explanation: Revelation 20:15 — "And anyone not found written in the Book of Life was cast into the lake of fire."

question: Complete the verse: "And He said to me, 'It is done! I am the _____ and the ____, the Beginning and the End. I will give of the fountain of the water of life freely to him who thirsts.'"
explanation: Revelation 21:6 — "It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End."

question: Which names are written on the twelve gates of the great city, the Holy Jerusalem?
explanation: Revelation 21:12 — "It had a great and high wall with twelve gates, and twelve angels at the gates, and names written on them, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel."

question: What was written on the twelve foundations of the wall of the city of Holy Jerusalem?

options.label: A
options.text: The names of the twelve patriarchs

options.label: B
options.text: The names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb

options.label: C
options.text: The names of the twelve prophets

options.label: D
options.text: The names of the twelve kings

answer_text: The names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb
explanation: Revelation 21:14 — "Now the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb."

question: "The Holy Jerusalem is laid out as a square; its length is as great as its breadth. And he measured the city with the reed: _______ Its length, breadth, and height are equal."
explanation: Revelation 21:16 — "And he measured the city with the reed: twelve thousand furlongs. Its length, breadth, and height are equal."

question: Who is the eldest among the two? Aaron Moses
explanation: Exodus 7:7 — "Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh." Aaron was three years older than Moses.

question: Who was the 1st judge of Israel?
explanation: Judges 3:9--10 — "Othniel the son of Kenaz ... became judge of Israel and went out to war."

question: Genesis 19:22 Escape there quickly, for I can do nothing
answer_text: Lot escaped to Zoar just as the sun rose over the earth, after the angel told him God could do nothing until he reached safety (Genesis 19:22-23).
explanation: Genesis 19:22--23 — Lot escaped to Zoar just as the sun rose over the earth.

question: On how many occasions did Abraham present his wife Sarah as
explanation: Genesis 12:11--13 (with Pharaoh in Egypt) and Genesis 20:2 (with Abimelech of Gerar) — Abraham said Sarah was his sister on two occasions.

question: What does the title "King of Salem" signify in the Bible?
explanation: Hebrews 7:2 — "First being translated king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, meaning king of peace."
